title: GraphRAG Entity and Relationship CRUD
description:
The server shall provide full CRUD operations for explicit graph entity nodes and relationship edges, persisted in workspace-scoped EF Core tables. Entities shall have name, type, description, and extensible JSON metadata. Relationships shall link two entities with a typed, weighted, described edge. Deleting an entity shall cascade to all its relationships. All operations shall be available via REST endpoints, MCP tools, and REPL commands.


**Covered by:** `GraphRagController` (entity + relationship endpoints), `QBrainAi.GraphRag` (`GraphRagService` entity / relationship CRUD), `GraphEntityEntity`, `GraphRelationshipEntity`, `FwhMcpTools` (graphrag entity/relationship tools), `QBrainAi.Repl.Core` (graphrag command shapes)

title: Request workspace paths are interpreted by their own syntax
description: A server must interpret any request-supplied workspace path by its own syntax (drive letter, UNC, POSIX root), never by the host OS, so a Linux host accepts and stores Windows paths unchanged in meaning.

criteria.text: On a Linux host, C:\Users\fixture-user, C:/Users/fixture-user resolve to the same Windows identity; nothing is prefixed with the process cwd.
On a Windows host, /home/x stays a POSIX path.
Triage submit/status round-trips: getReport with the submitter's original path finds the report on a Linux hub.
WorkspaceService.Init never creates a directory from a foreign-platform path.

When the workspace path belongs to the other platform and no Mcp:GitHub:Repository is configured, a GitHub CLI operation never starts gh and returns a failure that names the foreign workspace and the missing Mcp:GitHub:Repository setting; with a repository configured, gh runs with --repo and no working directory (operator 2026-10-29: "gh foreign-workspace AC (Recommended)"; holistic review findings SRC-1 and SRC-4).

notes: Registered in this workspace store 2026-10-19 by operator decision ("Create the records here now"). Statement and FR criteria verbatim from docs/plans/2026-10-07-federation-fixes.md:53-59 (approved 2026-10-07; first registered in the original Windows workspace store). Architecture Amendment 1 H0 import must merge with these records.

title: Global and workspace memory storage
description: The QBrain.AI SHALL store raw-text memories with a stable memory ID, explicit scope, and exact text round-trip semantics. Supported scopes are Global and Workspace. Global memories are visible to every workspace, while Workspace memories are visible only to their owning workspace.

criteria.text: A memory record has a stable ID, scope, category, raw text, version, author metadata, and created/updated timestamps.
Global memories are returned for every workspace and are not stamped with a workspace owner.
Workspace memories require an owning workspace and are not returned for any other workspace.
Removed memories are hidden from normal reads and lists without physically deleting the row.
Memory text round-trips exactly, including internal newlines and punctuation.

title: Memory CRUD tools
description: The QBrain.AI SHALL expose add, list, update, and remove operations for raw-text memories through REST, typed client, MCP stdio, and REPL workflow surfaces.

criteria.text: Add creates a memory and returns ID, text, scope, category, version, and timestamps.
List returns the effective memory set for the active workspace by default.
Update replaces raw text, increments version, and can change scope under validated rules.
Remove soft-deletes a memory by ID.
Invalid IDs, duplicate active IDs, invalid scopes, empty text, and unauthorized scope changes return clear errors.

title: QuadBrain OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint
description: QuadBrain SHALL expose an inbound OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint (chat/completions shape) backed by QuadBrain orchestration, accepting standard OpenAI chat messages and tool/function definitions and returning OpenAI-shaped completions - including assistant tool_calls when the model elects to invoke a tool - so any OpenAI-compatible client, including QBAgent, can use QuadBrain as a drop-in model. QBAgent (FR-MCP-QBAGENT-001) consumes this endpoint as its IChatClient and executes the emitted tool calls via the Microsoft Agent Framework loop; the ACID tightly-coupled profile is NOT required for QBAgent.

criteria.text: An inbound OpenAI chat request maps the role-tagged transcript onto QuadBrain orchestration and returns the Arbiter output as the assistant message.
Tool definitions in the request flow through and the response emits assistant tool_calls when QuadBrain elects to call a tool.
Bearer-auth (Authorization Bearer with X-Api-Key fallback) is validated via WorkspaceTokenService; invalid or missing yields 401.
QBAgent wires a standard OpenAI IChatClient to the v1 endpoint and runs the Agent Framework tool loop with action tools under the non-ACID profile.

With no tools in the request and no tool_choice, an Arbiter reply that is not an arbiter envelope is the final answer after one orchestration round and is returned as the assistant message with finish reason stop; an explicit continue envelope still asks for another round (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13; operator decision 2026-10-15 "Both rules (Recommended)"). A tool_choice of auto with no tools counts as no tool_choice, and a committed Arbiter output that is empty is answered with the no-decision message after one round (operator 2026-10-29: "QuadBrain ACs (Recommended)"; holistic review finding SRC-3).

When the round budget (8 orchestration rounds) ends without a final envelope, the response carries the last Arbiter output formatted for display as the assistant message with finish reason stop, never empty content; a last output whose display formatting leaves nothing (an Arbiter envelope without displayable content, or any other output that formats to nothing), and a budget that ends after an internal-tool round, are answered as ac-7 states (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13; operator decision 2026-10-15 "Both rules (Recommended)"; operator 2026-10-30: "F2: ac-6 vs ac-7 (Recommended)"; operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen ac-6 (Recommended)").

The assistant content is never an Arbiter envelope without displayable content: when display formatting of the answer leaves nothing, the content is a plain message naming the round budget and the last intent, and when the round budget ends after an internal-tool round, the content is that round's internal tool results (operator 2026-10-29: "QuadBrain ACs (Recommended)"; holistic review finding SRC-2).

title: QuadBrain Ollama endpoint integration tests
description: QuadBrainOllamaEndpointIntegrationTests exercise the OpenAI-compatible QuadBrain endpoint against a real local Ollama server that OllamaServerFixture adopts or starts (FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002), proving FR-MCP-QBOPENAI-001 runs the normal Creativity, Logic and Arbiter workflow without faking the LLM calls, on Windows and on Linux once InstallOllama has provisioned Ollama (TR-MCP-NUKE-016).

criteria.text: ChatCompletions_LocalOllamaDefaultModel_TriggersNormalBrainSlots (prompts "Hello" and "Create Hello World in C++"): with the local Ollama default model assigned to all four slots, each prompt triggers the normal Creativity, Logic and Arbiter workflow through POST /v1/chat/completions and returns non-empty content; every brain call uses that model at the Ollama endpoint, and the session log captures the brain outputs on the turn.

QBAgentRunLoop_LocalOllamaDefaultModel_DisplaysQuadBrainResponse (prompt "Hello"): QBAgent displays the QuadBrain response it received, never a placeholder; its transcript names the model QuadBrain and the QBrainAi endpoint and never the Ollama model id or endpoint.
ChatCompletions_OpenAiCompatibleFieldVariants_AreLoggedToSessionTurn: content, reasoning and reasoning_content outputs are persisted to the turn's processing dialog.

The class runs against a real local Ollama: OllamaServerFixture adopts a server already answering or starts one from a discovered executable and stops only what it started (FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002); on the Linux lab host the executable is the one InstallOllama provisions (TR-MCP-NUKE-016; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13, triage-report-680916ed).

notes: Recorded 2026-10-15: the four tests and OllamaServerController cite this id, which the store never held (operator decision "Approve all three (Recommended)"; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13, triage-report-680916ed).

title: Single request-path normalization entry point
description: Introduce a single request-path normalization entry point (IWorkspacePathNormalizer backed by WorkspaceIdentityPath) with an injectable host-platform abstraction; all resolvers listed in section 1.2 use it. No direct Path.GetFullPath on request-supplied workspace paths outside it (enforced by an architecture test).

criteria.evidence: tests/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests/Storage/WorkspacePathNormalizerContractTests.cs (CombineResolvesRootRelativeWindowsSegmentAgainstDrive, CombineResolvesRootRelativeWindowsSegmentAgainstUncShare); WorkspacePathNormalizerMockDataTests.cs (RootRelativeNegativeControls_AreRejectedInsidePassingHarness); PR 82 commits f6768359 and dcd0269a
criteria.text: IWorkspacePathNormalizer.Combine treats a segment with one leading backslash as root-relative on Windows: it keeps the current root's volume, the drive (C:/) or the UNC server and share (//srv/share/), and replaces the rest of the path, on a Linux hub and a Windows host (PR 81 finding P12, PR 82 review).

title: Hostile review execution capture
description:
ReviewExecution entity stores model string, effort, agent, plugin/source, template id/version, run id, start/end UTC. Token counts are optional and must not be invented.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003; TEST: TEST-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003

criteria.text: Invalid HostileReviewWorker options fail host startup with an error that names HostileReviewWorker, on Linux and on Windows: RenewalInterval not less than LeaseDuration; MaximumActiveQueue, MaximumConcurrentReviews or MaximumAttempts below 1. AgentName, RequiredModel and RequiredEffort are not startup rules: none is pinned, and an unset one means the default (operator rule 2026-10-15; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B9). The test host owns its logging providers, so an account that cannot write the Windows Application event log cannot turn the startup failure into a logging error (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B4, triage-report-f4d47e1f, measured on the Windows lab host 2026-10-15; HostileReviewStartupAssertion_AcceptsWorkerFailureAndRejectsMaskedOrMissing, HostileReviewWorker_InvalidOptions_FailStartup, HostileReviewWorkerOptions_AnyAgentModelEffort_PassValidation).

A reviewer output is accepted with the model and effort it reports, and the execution records them, when HostileReviewWorker RequiredModel and RequiredEffort are not configured; a configured RequiredModel or RequiredEffort is required of the output, and an output reporting a different value fails the request as ModelUnavailable (operator rule 2026-10-15; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B9; tests: WorkerOptionsAndOutputRules_AcceptUnpinnedOrConfiguredAndRejectPinsOrIgnoredConfig, AcceptReviewerOutput_NoConfiguredModel_RecordsReportedModel, AcceptReviewerOutput_ConfiguredModelMismatch_FailsModelUnavailable). An output that omits the reviewer agent, model or effort records them empty (not reported), never a default model (operator decision 2026-10-15 "Empty defaults, in B9"; test: AcceptReviewerOutput_NoConfiguredModel_RecordsReportedModel).
